name: Houlihan Lokey, Inc.
moat_justification: No. 1 global M&A advisor by deal count and No. 1 global restructuring franchise, with a three-segment mix (Corporate Finance, countercyclical Financial Restructuring, Financial & Valuation Advisory) that kept ROIC at 24-35% in every one of the last five fiscal years including the FY2023-24 deal trough — but it is a people business: no contracts or switching costs per mandate, managing directors can walk, and a ~61.5% compensation ratio means the bankers capture most of the economics.
fragility_flags: OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md

SBC_TAG_RECONCILED: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense exceeds ShareBasedCompensation for FY2017 (39,357,000 vs 45,059,000, +14.5%); the Allocated figure was used — the Share tag carries only part of stock compensation at this filer (a difference under 1% is tag rounding and needs one line in the analysis)
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.3x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.3%) vs bull-case tier C (12.0%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Premier mid-market advisory franchise, moat 6/10 — but at $130.33 the price pays full price for peak-cycle earnings: weighted IRR 9.2% (Tier D) on the $7.02 normalized base with TTM OE already down to $4.15/share, and it clears 15% only at or below $67.66.
moat_for: No. 1 global M&A advisor by transaction count and No. 1 global restructuring franchise (11 years) — scale and reputation in the mid-market segment bulge brackets underserve
Countercyclical mix: restructuring and valuation work offsets M&A downturns (FY2023 revenue fell 20% while M&A froze, and the firm stayed solidly profitable)
ROIC proxy 24.0-34.5% across FY2024-26 and 29.8% even in trough FY2023 — returns stayed well above cost of capital through the cycle
Asset-light, debt-free balance sheet: $1,189,454,000 cash at FY2026 against no filed funded debt — no balance-sheet risk to the franchise
Gross margin held in a 29.8-35.0% band over FY2022-25 despite the cycle — fee pricing power in its niches
moat_against: People business: clients hire individuals, not the platform — managing-director departures take revenue with them and there are no contracts or switching costs per mandate
Bankers capture the economics: adjusted compensation ratio guided to the 61.5% long-term target for FY2027, capping shareholder margin leverage
Deal fees are cyclical and closing-dependent: Q1 FY2027 Corporate Finance revenue fell to $303M from $398M on delayed larger-fee closings (Middle East instability, software-sector disruption)
Intense competition from bulge brackets moving downmarket and boutiques (Evercore, Moelis, Lazard) moving into the mid-market
Stock compensation is large and rising ($201,304,000 in FY2026) — a real, recurring cost of retaining the talent that is the moat
